newsitem.title: FINLAND: METSA-SERLA SEES BETTER H2 PROFITABILITY.
newsitem.headline: METSA-SERLA SEES BETTER H2 PROFITABILITY.

text.p: Finnish forestry group Metsa-Serla Oy said on Monday it saw favourable profitability in the second half of 1997.

"The Metsa-Serla management team believe in the company's favourable profitability development during the second half of 1997, providing the positive market development continues," Metsa-Serla said in a statement.
"The market for magazine papers is now improving, and both prices and profitability are expected to be better during the second quarter," it said.
Metsa-Serla said market pulp producers had cut production at the start of the second quarter so stocks would fall and prices rise before the summer.
However, it warned that "if prices are successfully increased, the latter part of the year might see growth in production and oversupply."
"The market situation (overall) has not improved during the first quarter ... there are some signs of improvement," Metsa-Serla said.
Demand for fine papers was expected to slacken, at least temporarily, in the second quarter, Metsa-Serla said.
Metsa-Serla said sales volume and profitability had improved considerably at its Swiss Biberist fine paper mill, acquired at the turn of the year.
Marketing of Biberist products would be integrated into Metsa-Serla's sales organisation during the second quarter.
Demand for corrugated board boxes was expected to grow in Finland, Denmark and the St Petersburg area in Russia, but prices would remain stable in the main markets, Metsa-Serla said.
Average containerboard prices were expected to strengthen "during the summer at the latest," it said.
